description: Side effect: connects the project to the user's Postgres or Supabase database and installs Dreamlit's schema and triggers in it. Use only when the person asks you to connect the database; normally get_setup_status directs them to connect on the setup page. Connect the database that holds the app's real users. Only after the user said yes in reply to the appropriate database consent question; never in the same turn you ask. Without a connection string, returns a link the user opens to connect in the browser (for Supabase, by signing in; no string needed). A database on the user's computer or private network can't be reached. Returns the connection status, usesLimitedRole (from the username), and the next setup step. Does not read or change the user's app data. Lead with the setup page returned by get_setup_status: explain how Dreamlit uses the database, ask the person to connect there, and check get_setup_status when they say it is done. Optionally offer: "If you'd rather, I can connect it from here." Only if the person asks you to connect it does the following path apply. Before setting up a database login or calling connect_database, tell the user in a line or two, in plain words, how Dreamlit uses the database (Dreamlit works straight from the app's database, so it stays the source of truth: no syncing data to another tool and no tracking events to add. It reads the tables to know who should get each email and to fill it in with their real details, reacts as things change in the app (a new signup, an upgrade, a cancelled plan), and never changes the app's data. Nothing reaches users until they approve an email.) Then ask if you may set this up, in your own plain words. For Supabase (a supabase.co or pooler.supabase.com host, a Supabase MCP server or CLI, or an audit database note identifying Supabase), say: "To connect, you'll sign in to Supabase in your browser and pick this project. Dreamlit then sets up its own login that can read your tables but can't change your data. Want the link?" End your message with that question and wait for a yes in a later message, never in the same turn you ask. After that yes, call connect_database without a connection string and give the person the link; when they say it's done, call get_setup_status. Do not run get_database_role_setup or build or pass a Supabase connection string. Supabase sign-in is the supported path: it lets Dreamlit read auth.users and run Supabase Auth workflows. For Postgres that isn't Supabase (including Neon, RDS, Railway and Render), ask: "To connect, I'll create a separate database login for Dreamlit that can read your tables but can't change your data, and give Dreamlit only that login. Your own database password stays on this machine. OK to set that up on <host> / <database>?" End your message with that question and wait; create the login and connect only after they say yes in a later message, never in the same turn you ask. After that yes: get_database_role_setup → run its SQL locally → connect_database with the dreamlit_app connection string → get_setup_status. Get the table-owner role from SELECT current_user or the table owner. Generate a letters-and-digits password locally (for example openssl rand -hex 24), substitute [[REPLACE_WITH_PASSWORD]] locally, and run the transactional script with psql or your database MCP SQL tool using the access you already have. Build the limited connection string locally with username dreamlit_app and the same host, port and database. Never print the password or either connection string, or send the owner password to Dreamlit. If you can't run SQL, the host refuses CREATE ROLE, or the person declines the script, explain that in one line and offer either connecting with the app's own login after a second explicit yes or connect_database without a string for the browser link; never fall back silently. If connect_database returns usesLimitedRole=false, tell the person plainly: "Dreamlit is connected with your app's own database login." If its result includes a Supabase sign-in notice, relay it.

connectionString.description: For Postgres that isn't Supabase, the dreamlit_app connection string created locally after get_database_role_setup. Send it only after the user agreed to setting up that host and database. The app's own login is also accepted, but requires a second explicit yes after explaining the fallback. Omit it to get a link the user can open instead; for Supabase that link connects by signing in, with no connection string.

projectId.description: Optional project id. Omit it when the workspace has one project.

name: connect_database

result.description: Dreamlit MCP result. success responses contain data and appUrls when relevant; auth_required, clarification_required, confirmation_required, handoff_required, and error responses explain the next action.

candidateColumns.description: Columns in the connected database that may split customers into groups (table.column).

expectedEditableVersionId.description: Editable version id returned by prepare_publish, used as a safety check.

expectedPublishedVersionId.description: Published version id returned by prepare_publish, used as a safety check.

expectedUpdatedAtIso.description: Workflow updatedAt timestamp returned by prepare_publish, used as a safety check.

isSandboxed.description: Whether to publish in sandbox mode so notifications are held for inspection.

messageType.description: Optional message type filter when selecting a draft message to test.

rowData.description: Optional sample data for rendering draft message variables during the test. If omitted, Dreamlit uses the same default preview data as the web builder when available.

testRecipientEmail.description: Optional recipient for email tests. If omitted, Dreamlit sends to the authenticated user's email address.

testTargetId.description: Structured test target id from testableMessages. Do not show this id to users; ask them to choose by message label.

workflowId.description: Workflow id whose editable draft message should be tested.

blocker.description: Why Dreamlit stopped before finishing the draft. Changes counted in appliedActionCount are already saved.

code.description: step_needs_detail: answer `detail` in a follow-up create_or_update_workflow call with the same workflowId. step_not_editable: change a different step instead. step_not_built: retry once, then finish in the browser. request_unclear: describe the change in more detail and retry.

detail.description: The specific missing detail or blocking rule, in plain language.

billingUrl.description: quota_exceeded or plan_upgrade_required: page where a workspace admin can buy AI credits or upgrade the plan.

helpUrl.description: Guide or support contact for resolving the problem in the message.

requestId.description: dreamlit_error: a reference for this failure. Give it to the user if it keeps failing.

resetAt.description: quota_exceeded: when this month's AI usage resets (ISO 8601).

retryable.description: dreamlit_error: the same call can work if tried again later.

stepEdits.description: edit_workflow_steps: what happened to each edit when none could be applied.

code.description: step_not_found: get fresh step ids from get_workflow_and_preview_url. step_not_editable: triggers can't be edited here; use create_or_update_workflow. field_not_for_step_type: send only fields for that step's type. duplicate_step: combine edits to one step. invalid_value: fix the value as the message says. query_failed: fix the SQL. query_drops_used_fields: keep returning fields, or edit the steps that use them in the same call. related_edit_failed: a related edit in this call (a SQL edit above or below this step) failed; fix it and send both again. save_failed: try again.

fields.description: query_drops_used_fields: fields later steps still use that the new query no longer returns.

index.description: Position of the edit in the request.

unreadableTables.description: table_rows_hidden_by_rls: tables Dreamlit can see but not read rows from, each with fixSql that adds Dreamlit's read policy. Run fixSql, or ask the user to run it, in the Supabase SQL editor, then try again.

title: Connect database
